## This run specifically

Implement GitHub issue #19 — "Chat turn is stranded as thinking when the MCP config write throws".
https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/19

`runTurn` in `src/lib/chat.ts` marks the session `thinking` and writes the MCP config before it constructs the promise it returns. A throw in that window leaves `chat_sessions.status = 'thinking'` for ever: `sendChatMessage` then refuses to send into the thread, and only a server restart clears it.

Done looks like: any failure between claiming the turn and handing back the promise settles the session back out of `thinking` and surfaces the error to the thread, with a regression test that fails before the change and passes after. Every acceptance-criteria box in the issue holds.

Scope note: issues #20, #22, #23 and #25 are also open against `src/lib/chat.ts` and may be running in parallel on their own branches — #20 in particular touches the same `runTurn` function, on how the turn settles. Fix only the pre-promise failure path named in this issue, keep the diff minimal, and do not restructure `runTurn` or add a general recovery path (that is #22's job). Note anything adjacent in your report instead of fixing it.
finalText:
Clean — the test wrote nothing into the repo and left no temp directories behind.

## What changed

`src/lib/chat.ts`, three places:

- **`sendChatMessage` (`chat.ts:617-638`)** — the `void runTurn(...).catch(...)` call is now inside a `try`/`catch`. `runTurn` is not `async`, so a throw from its pre-promise setup lands here rather than in the `.catch`. The handler records the failure through the same `finishTurn` the spawn-error path uses and returns `{ ok: false, reason }`, which the existing route turns into a 400 with the reason.
- **`runTurn` (`chat.ts:653-665`)** — `writeMcpConfig` is wrapped so a failure revokes the capability it just minted before rethrowing. `revokeCapability` is otherwise only reachable through `land`, inside the promise that failure never reaches, so the token would stay live for an hour.
- **`writeMcpConfig` (`chat.ts:1075-1100`)** — a failing `writeFileSync` best-effort unlinks the file before rethrowing. A part-written file (ENOSPC) carries the capability token and nothing else would ever remove it.

`CLAUDE.md` — the test-list paragraph now names `chatTurn.test.ts` and says why it is a second file and the only test that opens the database.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How checked |
|---|---|
| Row ends `failed` with the underlying error, not `thinking` | Asserted in the new test: `status === "failed"`, error matches both `/Could not start the turn/` and `/ENOENT/` |
| POST reports the failure rather than 500ing | `sendChatMessage` returns `{ ok: false, reason }`; `src/app/api/chat/[id]/message/route.ts:23-26` already maps that to a 400 with the reason. Asserted at the `sendChatMessage` boundary, not through an HTTP request |
| Capability revoked, config file unlinked | Revocation asserted (`__ufChatCaps.size === 0` after the failed turn). The unlink is **not** exercised by a test — forcing a mid-write failure that leaves a file behind needs `fs` patched, and in the ENOENT reproduction no file is created |
| Regression test failing before, passing after | Confirmed both directions, see below |

## Verification

```
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev   # ok
npm run typecheck                            # ok, no output
npm test                                     # 221 tests, 221 pass, 0 fail
```

Both directions of the regression test, by `git stash`ing only `src/lib/chat.ts`:

- **without the fix** — `not ok 1 - leaves the row failed, not thinking, and says why`, `error: "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/uf-chat-turn-…/no-such-directory/uf-mcp-….json'"`; 220 pass, 1 fail. The throw escapes `sendChatMessage` exactly as the issue describes.
- **with the fix** — 221 pass.

`npm run build` not run: nothing under `src/app/` or the build config changed. The issue's manual reproduction (a live server with `TMPDIR` pointed somewhere unwritable) is **unverified** — Docker is unavailable here and it needs a running server. The command a human should run is `TMPDIR=/proc/self npm run dev`, then send a chat message: expect a 400 with the reason and a thread that accepts the next message.

## Left alone

- `finishTurn` binds `r.sessionId` as `undefined` into a `COALESCE(?, session_id)` parameter on the failure paths. It works (the new test exercises it), but it relies on better-sqlite3 accepting `undefined` for a positional bind — worth a look, unrelated to this issue.
- The adjacent settling behaviour in `runTurn` (issue #20) and a general recovery path (#22) are untouched, per the scope note.

DONE
